claims.statement: Opening narrative calls Wei Jiu Wei Bao's elder brother (兄); King of Han later calls Wei Bao Wei Jiu's younger paternal cousin (從弟).

translationRepairs: In the winter of the fourth year of Han, when the King of Xiang and the King of Han were facing each other at Xingyang, Peng Yue attacked and took Suiyang, Waihuang, and seventeen other cities.
In the winter of the fourth year of Han, when the King of Xiang and the King of Han were facing each other at Xingyang, Peng Yue attacked and took seventeen cities including Suiyang and Waihuang.

睢陽、外黃十七城 names Suiyang and Waihuang as exemplars within a total of seventeen cities. Adding “other” invents nineteen captures; the proposed literal matches the Chinese count and the idiomatic field’s “seventeen cities, including…”.
